shortDescription: A short, mobile-friendly estimate-request form that emails you directly. Spam-protected. Structured for trade work — job address, what's broken, urgency, optional photos.
lead: A simple estimate-request form that lands in your inbox the second someone hits submit. No third-party directory taking a cut, no spam flood, no logging in to a marketplace to see who reached out. The form is built around the realities of trade work: name, contact preference, what trade or service they need, the job address (or just town if they're not ready to share it), urgency, and an optional photo upload so you can see the leak, the dent, or the busted panel before you drive out.

sections.heading: What You Get
sections.intro: A practical estimate-request form tuned for trade businesses — not a generic contact form. The right surface for first contact, with enough structure to triage between jobs.

items.label: Built for trade work
items.body: Name, contact preference, trade or service needed, job address or town, urgency, short description — fields tuned for the questions you actually need answered before quoting

items.label: Mobile-first layout
items.body: Big buttons, easy keyboards, no scroll-to-submit frustrations

items.label: Optional photo upload
items.body: Customers attach pictures of the busted water heater or the rotted deck so you can scope before driving out

items.label: Emails to you directly
items.body: New estimate requests go straight to the email(s) you choose — solo inbox, dispatch address, or both

items.label: Spam protection
items.body: Built-in bot filtering so your inbox stays clean

items.label: Optional add-ons
items.body: Service-line dropdowns, service-area ZIP check, urgent-vs-routine toggle, residential-vs-commercial routing

sections.heading: Why This Matters
sections.body: Most trade businesses route web inquiries through a directory like Angi or HomeAdvisor that controls the relationship and adds another login — and takes a cut of every job:
items: Form submits go directly to email (or multiple inboxes) — no marketplace middleman
No login, no portal, no third-party fees on the work
Job photos arrive with the request so you can quote without a site visit when you don't need one
Works on any phone, including older Android
Easy to scan — you can read between jobs, on the truck, or at the supply house

sections.heading: Perfect For
sections.intro: Estimate-request forms are the cheapest part of a website to get wrong, and the most expensive thing to leave broken. If any of these are you, this fix pays for itself fast.

items.label: Form that silently drops requests
items.body: Someone hits submit, nothing happens, you never see the email. A real customer just bounced and you don't even know it. We test every submission path end-to-end.

items.label: Form with no useful info
items.body: Your current form just has "name" and "message," and every request comes in saying "need a quote" with no address, no urgency, no photo. You waste hours on phone tag. We tighten the fields so you can quote.

items.label: Tired of paying directories
items.body: Angi, HomeAdvisor, Houzz, Thumbtack — they take a slice of your visibility every month and route requests through their own portal. Your own form keeps the whole job.

items.label: Solo operator, inbox between jobs
items.body: You have ten minutes between jobs. You don't have time to log into a portal. You want an email the moment a request comes in so you can reply before the day ends.

items.label: Drowning in unstructured requests
items.body: Requests come in from your personal email, voicemail, the form, and three different directories. You want everything funneled into one inbox so triage is consistent.

faqs.question: What information does the form actually capture?
faqs.answer: Name, contact preference (phone/text/email), trade or service needed, job address or town, urgency (emergency, this week, flexible), a short description, and optional photo upload. We tune the exact fields to your trade — a plumber's form will look slightly different from a finish carpenter's.

faqs.question: Do you have spam protection on the form?
faqs.answer: Yes. We use bot-filtering that doesn't make a real customer solve a puzzle. Most spam never lands in your inbox; what slips through is rare and easy to spot.

faqs.question: Will the form work on phones — including older Androids?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mobile-first is the default — big tap targets, sensible keyboard types per field, no scroll-to-submit frustrations. We test on real devices, not just emulators.

faqs.question: Can submissions go to multiple people in a multi-crew shop?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send to a single dispatch address, multiple crew leads, or route by service if you want, say, HVAC requests going to one address and plumbing to another.

faqs.question: Where do submissions actually go — is there a portal?
faqs.answer: No portal — submissions arrive as a regular email in your inbox the second a customer hits submit. No login. No app. Just email.
